report: PyShield Round 3 fourth-material review (invitation + fix response)
verdict_reason: The invitation is structurally accurate and the main R4 fixes verify, but the current challenge zip ships __pycache__ entries outside the signed manifest and check_release.py neither rejects them nor scans master/build keys in --temp or archives without a sibling secret.

findings.title: Challenge zip ships __pycache__ outside the signed manifest; a tampered pyc executes while the manifest passes
findings.preconditions: local write access to the deployment directory; challenge zip already contains __pycache__; no admin/debugger/memory dump required
findings.summary: The challenge zip contains demo/__pycache__ and related caches. demo/__init__.py is in the signed manifest, but its pycache is not. Replacing the pyc with code that matches the source mtime/size executes the marker while manage.py check and the signed manifest still pass.
findings.root_cause: The zip includes demo/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-312.pyc (and apps/urls/views/management/sampleproj caches). .pyshield-manifest.json has 23 entries and lists demo/__init__.py, but no pycache. _core.py:190-235 only hashes manifest entries; Python 3.12 trusts the pyc timestamp header. builder.py:1004 calls clean_pycache after verify, but the challenge zip was created after a post-build manage.py check, and check_release.py has no pycache rule.
repro_steps: Extract round3-django-shielded.zip and confirm demo/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-312.pyc exists.
Read demo/__init__.py mtime/size and build a pyc header with those values.
Write header + marshal.dumps(compile("print('PYSHELD_PYC_BYPASS')", 'demo/__init__.py', 'exec')) over the pycache entry.
findings.impact: Arbitrary code execution in the app process and a bypass of the manifest's tamper-detection claim; the code can patch runtime/license/clock state after startup. It is not necessarily a cold-start license bypass for an already-expired license, because the initial license check may run before demo/__init__.py is imported.
evidence: logs/pycache-tamper.log: PYSHELD_PYC_BYPASS printed; System check identified no issues; returncode 0
logs/challenge-zip-list.log: demo/__pycache__ and management/sampleproj __pycache__ entries present
manifest: 23 entries, demo/__init__.py listed, zero pycache entries
findings.remediation: Remove all __pycache__/non-runtime pyc from the challenge zip and every release; reject unexpected pycache in check_release.py and at runtime; add pycache paths to the signed manifest or reject them; set sys.pycache_prefix to a temp dir before importing protected modules; add a tamper regression test.
findings.post_fix_verification: pycache_tamper.py must fail closed (LicenseError/integrity failure) and check_release.py must reject a zip containing __pycache__; flag recovery and manage.py check must still pass after cache removal.
findings.residual_risk: A local user who can write the release tree can still replace unprotected files or the whole runtime; this fix removes the accidental executable cache path.

findings.title: check_release.py does not scan master/build keys in --temp or archives without a sibling secret, and does not reject pycache
findings.preconditions: release/build process relies on check_release.py; local user; no active secret leak required to demonstrate the false negative
findings.summary: --temp passes an empty key-needle tuple for ordinary files; a zip without a sibling *.shield-secret.json has no key needles; __pycache__ is not rejected. A test master/build key in a pyshield* TEMP dir and in a zip both passed, and the current pycache-containing challenge zip also passed.
findings.root_cause: tools/check_release.py: _scan_temp calls _scan_bytes(..., needles=()) at :132ff; _scan_target derives needles only from licensing.secret_path_for(target) at :104ff; _scan_zip at :84ff scans bytes and .shield-secret.json names but has no pycache rule; _scan_bytes checks flag/PEM/needles only.
repro_steps: Derive the authorized sample's master/build key (test key) and write a pyshield-check-gap-* TEMP directory containing master.txt with the key hex.
Run python tools/check_release.py --temp: exit 0, no key detection.
Create a zip without a sibling secret containing master.txt; run check_release.py <zip>: exit 0.
Run check_release.py on the current challenge zip with __pycache__: exit 0.
findings.impact: False assurance: a real master/build key in TEMP or in an archive without a sibling secret can pass; current artifacts/temp had no such leak, so this is a coverage/claim defect, not an observed compromise. It also allows PSH-R5-001's pycache zip to pass release hygiene.
evidence: logs/check-release-gap.log: TEMP result 0 and ZIP result 0 with a real test master/build key
logs/check-release-challenge.log: current challenge zip returns release check OK despite __pycache__
tools/check_release.py: --temp uses needles=(); zip needles require sibling secret
findings.remediation: Add --secret <path> and discover siblings for archives; scan all TEMP entries, not only pyshield*/psh*; derive/test key needles for --temp; reject __pycache__ and unexpected .pyc; add regression tests for key files and pycache; qualify documentation.
findings.post_fix_verification: check_release_gap.py must exit non-zero in both TEMP and zip cases; check_release.py must fail on the pycache challenge zip; --temp must not claim master/build-key coverage without a provided secret.
findings.residual_risk: Release hygiene is process control; a specialized build account/machine is still recommended.
